quest.title: Storytelling Method
quest.description: Junkichi seems to be struggling with his writing again...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x100, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x6

dialogues.speaker: Junkichi
dialogues.text: ...So this is the structure I have in mind this time.

dialogues.speaker: Junkichi
dialogues.text: The supremely-skilled ninja uses all sorts of abilities to infiltrate the enemy fortress and retrieve the required intel in secret...

dialogues.speaker: Shigeru
dialogues.text: *sigh* And how many "abilities" are you going to give this ninja this time?

dialogues.speaker: Junkichi
dialogues.text: Th—That, uh, might depend on the situation?

dialogues.speaker: Shigeru
dialogues.text: Right. So you haven't thought about it, then.

dialogues.speaker: Junkichi
dialogues.text: I mean, it's fine! I mean, if you lock down all the narrative devices ahead of time, there's nowhere to adapt from there, right?

dialogues.speaker: Shigeru
dialogues.text: Oh, here you go again. If you had these devices locked in beforehand, your writing wouldn't go all over the shop!

dialogues.speaker: Junkichi
dialogues.text: I—I have my own creative methods, alright? The story should put its narrative first. How can it be shackled by these devices?

dialogues.speaker: Shigeru
dialogues.text: That's just irresponsible, you...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What are you two arguing about?

dialogues.speaker: Junkichi
dialogues.text: Oh, its you! I was just thinking about to structure a novel about a ninja.

dialogues.speaker: Junkichi
dialogues.text: But Shigeru's criticizing the structures that I came up with again...

dialogues.speaker: Shigeru
dialogues.text: I'm not saying that what you've come up with is bad, per se. I'm just asking you to put your narrative devices in place first before you start writing...

dialogues.speaker: Junkichi
dialogues.text: No, no... I'm not going to list them all down and structure the narrative around them. That's just too staid!

dialogues.speaker: Junkichi
dialogues.text: The narrative is the most important thing in the novel, which everything else revolves around, even the setting and narrative devices...

dialogues.speaker: Shigeru
dialogues.text: You...

response.speaker: Shigeru
response.text: Forget it, you're not going to listen to me anyway...

response.speaker: Junkichi
response.text: I'm sticking to my creative principles no matter what you say.

response.speaker: Shigeru
response.text: *sigh* ...You know what, Traveler? Since you're here, why don't you be the judge?

choices.text: And how am I supposed to judge...

response.speaker: Shigeru
response.text: Uh, no, you just need to listen to Junkichi tell us the structure of this new narrative passage he's dreamed up.

response.speaker: Shigeru
response.text: After that, just use your judgment and think about how his ninja would act.

response.speaker: Shigeru
response.text: That way, Junkichi should get the feedback he needs about what happens when he just writes his story willy-nilly.

response.speaker: Junkichi
response.text: Hmph, sure. Well, Traveler, we're counting on you.

response.speaker: Junkichi
response.text: I'll narrate the story for you. Just act according to what you think is natural.

response.speaker: Junkichi
response.text: Let's show Shigeru how awesome a story unbound by these... narrative devices can be!

response.speaker: Junkichi
response.text: So, as I was writing, this ninja is entering the enemy fortress solo, preparing to steal critical intelligence.

response.speaker: Junkichi
response.text: Hehe, Traveler, are you ready to play the stealthy ninja?

response.speaker: Junkichi
response.text: Having made all the necessary preparations, the ninja infiltrates the fortress stealthily...

choices.text: This creativity business sure is tiring...
Am I supposed to read his novel right here and now?
Let's call a halt to this real quick, shall we?

talks.objective: Get a feel for Junkichi's story

dialogues.speaker: Junkichi
dialogues.text: Alright, that's a wrap.

dialogues.speaker: Junkichi
dialogues.text: I've... never been this tired. Was this story always that complicated...

dialogues.speaker: Shigeru
dialogues.text: That's what you get when you don't decide on things early. Without narrative devices to restrain you, the various elements just clash wildly against each other.

dialogues.speaker: Shigeru
dialogues.text: When that happens, you'll end up losing control over the plot altogether. You'd exhaust yourself no matter what you were writing.

dialogues.speaker: Junkichi
dialogues.text: *sigh* Alright, alright... I've got no strength left to argue with you. Traveler, thanks for your... judgment.

dialogues.speaker: Junkichi
dialogues.text: I think I've gained a lot from this...

dialogues.speaker: Junkichi
dialogues.text: Take this as a token of my thanks. I'll get to writing again shortly.

dialogues.speaker: Junkichi
dialogues.text: Hmm, narrative devices or narrative... Which is more important?
